messages.subject: spark server usage limitations?
parts:
Hi,

   I've written  randomization apps in shiny which I'm having my students use.
http://spark.rstudio.com/jimrc/spin/  and http://spark.rstudio.com/jimrc/mix/
  
   Thanks for hosting this.  I really appreciate your work on shiny.
I am working toward getting these apps hosted locally at Montana State U, but our IT guy has other fires to put out, so it will be a while.
We have 250-300 students in the intro stats class, so I wonder if this is putting pressure on the system.
During our class times, we might have 15 people using the server.  At one point on Tu & THurs, it could be double that.
Is there a limit to our usage?
Sometimes  students are getting turned away from the server.  A few are getting a grayed out screen.

Again, I appreciate your hard work, and don't want to be taking advantage of this great resource.

Best,
Jim Robison-Cox

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: spark server usage limitations?
parts:
Hi Jim,

I like your apps! Thanks for your consideration regarding performance.

We currently have Spark configured to allow 200 concurrent users on each application before we'll start showing the "Server Overloaded" message. (This was a fairly recent change to Spark, however, so you may have found different performance patterns previously.) That being said, the user experience offered on most apps with 200 concurrent users won't be very pleasant; remember that R is single-threaded, so any time R is doing computation for one user, the other 199 would have be waiting.

They grayed out screen should be a rare byproduct of one of us doing work on the server -- we try to minimize that as much as possible. Are you seeing that more than, say, once a day?

All in all, if your application is computationally light enough to fluidly support 30 (or 50, or 100) simultaneous users, then you shouldn't find Spark to be limiting!

Jeff
